confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from four web searches that returned aggregated price indexes. Numbeo gave EUR 10.30 for an inexpensive meal, EUR 51.49 for a mid-range meal for two, EUR 3.70 for a cappuccino and EUR 3.43 for a draft beer. Expatistan and other aggregators gave about 15-17 zł for a 0.5 L beer. I converted these to USD with an approximate PLN/EUR-to-USD rate of my own, not a searched rate, so the conversion adds some error. Cocktail and wine anchors are the weakest food and drink figures. I found only a crowd-sourced club cocktail estimate of about 34 zł and a 2019 hotel-bar menu with 0.15 L wine glasses at about 19-38 PLN. I therefore set cocktail at roughly 2.3x the beer price and wine at roughly 1.5x, with an allowance for inflation since 2019. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for the July 2026 peak season. I did not search for or inspect any accommodation listings or booking pages. They could be off by 20-30% depending on location (Old Town and waterfront versus outer districts) and dates. The FX figure is the 18 Nov 2026 RBA 4.00 pm AUD/USD rate, found through a web search of RBA pages.
comparable_city_reasoning: Gdansk is priced as a mid-sized Polish tourist city, slightly above the national average and somewhat below Warsaw and Krakow in-season. Restaurant and drink anchors follow Numbeo and Expatistan figures for Gdansk itself. Accommodation is benchmarked against comparable Baltic and Central European summer-peak cities.
